name: Footwear manufacturing

problems.words: We have size 40 and 41 stuck while 42 and 43 sold out
quick_ideas: Count stock of your top articles by size once, so you see exactly which sizes are stuck
Write down last season's sales by size for those articles, so the next size mix is based on a record, not a guess

workzap_build.text: An article-size matrix showing pairs by article, colour and size across factory, godown and shops, with a daily read of sizes running out or piling up.

problems.ask_first: How do you see stock by size today?
problems.free_stops: How size mix is planned from sales history is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare pairs sent out by size with pairs left back for the same articles, so the wrong size mix shows clearly.
Give one storekeeper one shelf list for slow sizes by article, so replenishment stops repeating the same stuck sizes.

problems.words: Size sets get broken at the godown and dealers refuse half sets
quick_ideas: Count how many broken sets are sitting in the godown now, so you know the scale
Keep full-set cartons and loose pairs in separate marked areas, so sets stop being opened casually

workzap_build.text: Size-set carton packing with scan-in and scan-out, so every carton opened or moved is recorded.

problems.ask_first: Do sets get broken when dealers order loose sizes, or when your own staff open cartons at the godown?
problems.free_stops: How cartons are coded and scanned is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note how many cartons were opened in the godown to complete odd dealer requests this week, so you see what is breaking sets.
Give one person the job of approving any carton opening in one marked notebook, so full sets stay protected for dealers.

problems.words: Sole supplier delivers late and lasting stops
quick_ideas: Work out the soles needed for this month's planned pairs and share it with the supplier once, so they get real warning
Note the last few late deliveries and days lost, so the conversation uses facts

workzap_build.text: Material requirements worked out from planned pairs (soles, uppers, adhesive, boxes) with shortage alerts before lasting stops.

problems.free_stops: How requirements are calculated per article and size is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each day lasting waits for soles against the promised delivery day, so supplier delay is clear in lost production time.
Give one person one place to note sole needs and supplier promises, so lasting stops chasing material through scattered chats.

problems.words: Mould or press breaks and we lose days
quick_ideas: List every mould by article and size with its condition, so you know which are at risk
Note which moulds failed last season, so they are checked before the next peak

workzap_build.text: A mould register by article and size with condition and repair history, and a log of every press breakdown.

problems.ask_first: Does the breakdown usually hit a mould, or the press itself?
problems.free_stops: Inspection routine and repair priorities are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which moulds or presses stopped work most often this season, so attention goes to the equipment causing the longest interruptions.
Give one fitter one notebook for breakdowns and repairs by machine, so repeat faults are handed over clearly across shifts.

problems.words: Defects found only when dealers open cartons
quick_ideas: Put one person on a check before cartons close for sole bonding and finish, so faults are caught inside
Note the reasons for the last returns, so checking focuses on them

workzap_build.text: A pre-dispatch QC checklist with defect types and photos recorded for every lot.

problems.ask_first: Are the defects mostly in sole bonding, or in stitching and finish?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and how defects are traced to a stage are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count dealer complaints by defect type from the last cartons returned, so the missed checks match the faults actually reaching market.
Give one checker the carton closing signoff in one notebook, so faults are owned before goods leave the factory.

problems.words: Dealers take goods on credit and pay after the season
quick_ideas: Make one list of every dealer's balance and oldest bill, so you know where to start
Check that list before the next Eid dispatch, so credit does not keep stacking up

workzap_build.text: A dealer ledger with ageing, credit limits checked at order time and season-end return tracking.

problems.ask_first: Is the credit mostly with a few big dealers, or spread across many small shops?
problems.free_stops: How limits and return terms are tracked per dealer is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count pairs still lying ready for dealers who still owe from the last season, so blocked stock against blocked cash becomes visible.
Keep one season dues notebook at the dispatch table under one staff role, so every outgoing pair is checked against old balances.

problems.words: Pairs per worker are disputed every week (piece rate)
quick_ideas: Have the supervisor count and sign pairs per stage at day end for one week, so there is an agreed record
Show the count to each worker the same day, so disputes start small

workzap_build.text: Daily piece counts per worker role entered by supervisors, feeding a weekly count sheet everyone can see.

problems.ask_first: Do the disputes come from the count of pairs, or from which rate applies to each stage?
problems.free_stops: How counts are verified and fed into the weekly sheet is detailed in the solution document; for wage rules, talk to your lawyer or accountant.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the supervisor's daily pair count with each worker's claimed count for one week, so the counting gap shows.
Give one supervisor one end of day pair register by stage, so weekly piece counts are handed over from one record.

problems.words: Own shops' sales aren't visible to the factory until month end
quick_ideas: Ask each shop for one day-end sales count by article and size this week, so you see what is moving
Compare it with what was dispatched to them

workzap_build.text: Own-shop sales synced to the factory daily with size-level sell-through.

problems.ask_first: Do your own shops sit in one city, or are they spread across several?
problems.free_stops: How shop sales connect to factory stock is mapped in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each shop's fastest moving articles and sizes at day end for one week, so the factory sees demand before month closing.
Give one staff member one fixed evening time to collect shop counts in one notebook, so factory planning gets a steady sales picture.

problems.words: Daraz orders come in with the wrong size picked
quick_ideas: Keep a separate packing shelf for online orders, so they are not picked from mixed stock
Recheck size against the order before sealing, so errors are caught before dispatch

workzap_build.text: Online orders in one list with a pick check against article and size before dispatch.

problems.ask_first: Does the wrong size come from picking at the shelf, or from mislabelled cartons?
problems.free_stops: The pick-check flow is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count which articles and sizes had wrong picks this week, so you see whether the errors come from certain shelves or pairs.
Give one packer one handwritten online order list at packing time, so size checking happens from a single handover record.

problems.words: No planning for which articles to make next season
quick_ideas: List last season's articles with what sold out and what came back, so you start from facts
Mark which ones to repeat, drop or change

workzap_build.text: A season planning view comparing last season's sales by article and size.

problems.ask_first: Do you choose articles by feel at the start of the season, or from last season's sales list?
problems.free_stops: How the view turns into a production plan is detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many dealers asked again for each article after you ran out last season, so next season choices reflect missed demand.
Give one person one notebook for repeat, drop and change notes after dealer visits, so article planning stays together before the season.

never_say: Anything on safety-footwear certification or standards, or orthopaedic or medical fit claims.
Any help copying another brand's trademarks or logos, or making counterfeit goods.
Anything on adhesive or solvent handling; fumes causing collapse are emergencies.
Any judgement on fairness or legality of piece rates.
Any guarantee of sell-through or fewer returns.

sample_reply.person: Eid ke liye maal banaya tha, ab chhote size pare hain aur bare size khatam. Agli dafa yeh na ho, koi tareeqa batao.
sample_reply.pi:
Ji haan, ye theek ho sakta hai, aur pehla qadam aasan hai.
Pehle, apne main articles ka size-wise stock ek dafa gin lein, taa ke saaf ho kaun se size atke hue hain.
Doosra, pichle season ki size-wise sale likh lein, taa ke agla size mix record pe bane, andaaze pe nahi.
Workzap is ke liye ye bana sakta hai: factory, godown aur shops ka article aur size-wise stock ek jagah, aur har subah kaun sa size khatam ho raha hai woh aap ke WhatsApp pe.

Kya main aap ke liye solution document aur quote banwa doon? Mana bhi kar sakte hain.
